namelist_definition.entry: Default: ' ' Full pathname of the land domain (fraction) file. Set from the xml variables LND_DOMAIN_PATH and LND_DOMAIN_FILE. ELMXX reads the grid dimensions, cell center coordinates, cell areas, mask and land fraction from this file, and hands them to the coupler as the land domain.

Default: ' ' Full pathname of the surface dataset. ELMXX reads the subgrid composition (PCT_NATVEG, PCT_NAT_PFT, PCT_URBAN, PCT_LAKE, PCT_GLACIER, PCT_WETLAND, PCT_CROP), the soil properties (PCT_SAND, PCT_CLAY, ORGANIC, SOIL_COLOR, FMAX) and the satellite-phenology streams (MONTHLY_LAI, MONTHLY_SAI, MONTHLY_HEIGHT_TOP, MONTHLY_HEIGHT_BOT) from this file.
Unlike ELM, ELMXX has no -clm_usr_name machinery to derive this from a naming convention, so it must be set explicitly -- normally in user_nl_elmxx.

Default: .true. If .true., round-trip a per-entity fingerprint through the Kokkos views at the end of step 1 and check that every packed slot returns what was written to it. This validates the Fortran/Kokkos boundary plumbing: extents matching the views ELMxxCreate allocated, no setter silently rejected, both the int and double paths.
The map SEMANTICS -- bijection, landunit types, patch-to-column agreement -- are checked separately at init and are not controlled by this switch, because they need no Kokkos and cost nothing.

Default: .false. If .false., a boundary-check mismatch aborts the run. If .true., it is reported and the run continues.
Abort is the right default while the boundary is being brought up: a wrong index map is silent corruption and every kernel added later builds on it. Set .true. only when a long run must survive a known mismatch during kernel bring-up.

Default: '' (no kernels active) Comma-separated list of ELMxx Kokkos kernels to activate, in any order -- they always RUN in driver order, since each reads what the ones before it wrote. Valid names, in that driver order:
surfrad, canhydro, cansunshade, cantemp, baregrnd, canflux, urbanrad, urbanflux, lakeflux, laketemp, soiltemp, soilflux, surfrunoff, rootwater, hydrodrain, lakehydro
There is no Fortran alternative to switch away from: a kernel that is not named simply does not run, so the timestep stays incomplete until all of them are on. Intermediate runs are diagnostic only.
An unknown name aborts, and so does a name whose prerequisites are not met -- most kernels still need the Stage 5 albedo port or the iniTimeConst pedotransfer port. A kernel run on unset inputs would read zeros and produce plausible-looking garbage rather than failing, which is why this is enforced at init instead of being left to inspection.
